The **domain separator** (`domainSeparator = hashStruct(EIP712Domain)`) is the part of the digest that binds a signature to one contract and one chain.

The final digest is `keccak256("\x19\x01" ‖ domainSeparator ‖ hashStruct(message))`. The domain separator hashes the `EIP712Domain` struct, which includes:

- `chainId`, so a signature can't be replayed on another chain.
- `verifyingContract`, so it can't be replayed against another contract.
- `name` and `version`, plus an optional `salt`.

The `\x19\x01` prefix only keeps the digest from being read as a valid transaction or an EIP-191 message. The message struct hash covers the signed data itself. A per-user nonce, which is part of the message, stops replay on the same contract and chain.

If a chain forks, the cached separator can go stale. Good implementations recompute it when `block.chainid` changes.
